review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; self-review, not independent approval
review.decision: Close the inherited cross-publisher Codex resume-index race using the existing shared lease and a post-preparation snapshot check
review.notes: Read and SHA-verified independent REVIEW790e. Fresh main9318 still has bootstrap blob933f and reachable radar call. Audit: Save(codex), Bind, Refresh including index repair/checkpoint, and End index touch use codex-frontend-binding; completeCodexBinding and commitProcessBinding use only the per-location O_EXCL file. Keep existing eligibility, TTL, receipts, per-location legacy exclusion and atomic JSON writes. Prepare history outside the global lease, then acquire the same nonblocking kernel lease and re-read exact incumbent before publication/retirement; any field change defers rather than overwriting newer identity/checkpoint. Both newly covered publishers use one helper. Process same-owner updates preserve Frontend as well as TerminalClient. Lock order remains location O_EXCL then nonblocking global; no global holder acquires that location lock. Failure releases both, witnesses remain retryable. Explicit validation seam only at bootstrap checkpoint I/O, defaulting to original function; negative baseline is exact main plus this behavior-neutral seam, not a deployed binary or protocol-only toy. Actual public Go publishers perform reads, writes, Bind and Refresh in isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME. No production session/process/queue/frontend registry/service/TCC changes. Non-Codex Save retains its existing separate legacy ownership policy; Remove has no production caller in this tree and is administrative, not a Codex publisher. Old binaries ignoring the shared lease remain a rollout compatibility limit, not covered by a file rename. No claim these changes explain current HQ identity/queue symptoms. No worker or independent approval inferred.

cases.description: Actual bootstrap cannot overwrite a frontend published after its incumbent snapshot
cases.setup: Isolated real resume/intents/rollout files; existing synthetic strict foreground/birth sensors; actual Complete and Bind functions. A checkpoint I/O barrier pauses bootstrap after owner validation.
cases.action: Pause old bootstrap, successfully bind a new frontend to another session or the bootstrap destination session, release old checkpoint and inspect primary index, frontend receipt, intent and heartbeat.
cases.expected: Old baseline overwrites or strips the newer frontend; repaired source refuses stale publication, keeps the exact new primary/receipt, retains retry witness and leaves leases available. Same destination session does not justify dropping a newer frontend. No sleep/probability race.

cases.description: Bootstrap and process fallback obey the same cross-publisher kernel lease
cases.setup: Real temporary state lease held externally; actual Complete and public process reconcile/hook paths with isolated records and process sensors.
cases.action: Attempt each publication while the global lease is held, then retry normally after release.
cases.expected: Contention returns/defer without changing primary, receipts or intent. Eligible retry publishes only after a fresh exact index comparison. Both previously uncovered writer paths are covered; existing Save/Refresh CSR003 assertions remain untouched.

cases.description: Publication failures do not leak locks or lose owner/frontend/retry evidence
cases.setup: Isolated changed/missing intent, occupied legacy lock, record-path blocker and receipt-path blocker; same-owner verified frontend/process control.
cases.action: Run real publication paths, check explicit error/receipt-error and repeat after correcting fixture failure; verify a subsequent Bind/Refresh can acquire the lease.
cases.expected: Failure preserves incumbent and pending intent as appropriate; committed-index/failed-retirement remains explicitly retryable. No deadlock or leaked shared/location lock. Same owner retains Frontend and TerminalClient; changed owner cannot be reclaimed by retry. Existing valid assertions and budgets are not weakened.

cases.description: Cross-process lease excludes the actual bootstrap publisher
cases.setup: Parent holds real state lease; child is the same compiled test binary with only temporary synthetic HOME/CODEX_HOME and serialized fixture input.
cases.action: Run actual Complete in child while held and after release, with bounded child execution and full source snapshots.
cases.expected: Held lease prevents publication and consumption across OS processes; after release the exact valid fixture succeeds. No real state directory, target, backend or service is touched. Helper entry is not separate product acceptance.
